public_rationale: Apple disclosed both licensed datasets and web-crawled training data. That supports the narrower statement that its data was not obtained solely through negotiated licensing arrangements. It does not settle the licensing status of the crawled content. Treating all publicly accessible material as unlicensed would add an unsupported assumption. The cited disclosure therefore does not establish the stronger claim as written.
limitations: This assessment does not decide whether any training use infringed copyright.
The source has later updates; the cited training-data discussion concerns the models introduced in June 2024.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Apple has not trained its models only on licensed content.

statement.excerpt: While I’d love to believe that Apple has only used licensed content to train its models, that clearly isn’t the case, and if their version of “publicly available” includes things from Google, or DeviantArt, or social networks, Apple is willingly participating in the AI boom’s continual pillaging of the internet.

from_speaker: Apple has only used licensed content to train its models
our_interpretation: Assess the factual assertion about the training of the Apple Intelligence models discussed in the post.
Licensed includes applicable open licenses as well as individually negotiated licenses.
Public accessibility and collection by a crawler do not, by themselves, establish whether content was licensed.
The conditional speculation about particular websites and the moral characterization of pillaging are not separate factual commitments in the normalized claim.
The target is training completed by the post date; no training start date is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: A reliable disclosure or documented training record establishes inclusion of content used without an applicable license.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A sufficiently complete training-data and rights record establishes that all relevant training content was licensed.
